free_tier.stated: VPS 1 at $7.10 per month on the homepage, under Day / Month / Year terms (the site also names payment three years ahead): 15 GB SSD, 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 dedicated IP, Linux (AlmaLinux, CentOS, Debian, Ubuntu), in the Netherlands, Slovakia or Serbia. The billing panel's guest order view prices the plan per day (see the evidence rows); its full price list and any month or year cart prices sit behind registration, so the annual and renewal prices are not published on any page read; the plan is orderable (Order buttons, no out-of-stock marker). The vendor's KVM page states 'Traffic for your VPS is unlimited. This means you can host services or applications that require a high bandwidth at no extra cost.'

egress.terms: unlimited traffic in the vendor's words on the KVM page, with no allowance and no overage price stated; the tracker instead lists a 5,120 GB monthly figure
egress.free_allowance: unlimited, as stated on the vendor's KVM page

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with billing at bill.vps1.net; the site exposes a status page and an IP-pool page. No API was read.
chaining: Fifteen gigabytes of SSD, 1 GB of RAM and a claimed unlimited transfer for $7.10 across three central-European countries is a plausible always-on egress or relay point if the unlimited claim survives a test; the 15 GB disk is the wall that stops it being anything more.
limits_note: No monthly byte allowance is stated on either vendor page read; the KVM page states unlimited traffic outright. That conflicts with the tracker's 5,120 GB/month and 0.24 Gbps, and the conflict is left standing rather than averaged into a figure neither source gave. If the vendor's unlimited claim holds, the wall is the 15 GB disk and whatever port rate the plan actually has, which no vendor page read states.
